arxiv-1511-03693.title: Game characterizations and lower cones in the Weihrauch degrees Thanks: This research was partially done whilst the authors were visiting fellows at the Isaac Newton Institute for Mathematical Sciences in the programme ‘Mathematical, Foundational and Computational Aspects of the Higher Infinite’. Th
arxiv-1511-03693.creator: Hugo Nobrega, Arno Pauly
arxiv-1511-03693.description: Abstract . We introduce a parametrized version of the Wadge game for functions and show that each lower cone in the Weihrauch degrees is characterized by such a game. These parametrized Wadge games subsume the original Wadge game, the eraser and backtrack games as well as Semmes’s tree games.

arxiv-2012-12627.title: Bridging Textual and Tabular Data for Cross-Domain Text-to-SQL Semantic Parsing
arxiv-2012-12627.creator: Xi Victoria Lin, Richard Socher, Caiming Xiong
arxiv-2012-12627.description: Abstract We present BRIDGE, a powerful sequential architecture for modeling dependencies between natural language questions and relational databases in cross-DB semantic parsing. BRIDGE represents the question and DB schema in a tagged sequence where a subset of the fields are augmented with cell values mentioned in the question.

arxiv-2202-02890.title: Rates of convergence for nonparametric estimation of singular distributions using generative adversarial networks
arxiv-2202-02890.creator: Minwoo Chae
arxiv-2202-02890.description: Abstract We consider generative adversarial networks (GAN) for estimating parameters in a deep generative model. The data-generating distribution is assumed to concentrate around some low-dimensional structure, making the target distribution singular to the Lebesgue measure. Under this assumption, we obtain convergence rates of a GAN type estimator with respect to the Wasserstein metric.

arxiv-2409-17615.title: Entropy scaling for diffusion coefficients in fluid mixtures
arxiv-2409-17615.creator: Sebastian Schmitt, Hans Hasse, Simon Stephan
arxiv-2409-17615.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Sebastian Schmitt, Hans Hasse, Simon Stephan. Entropy scaling is a powerful technique that has been used for predicting transport properties of pure components over a wide range of states. However, modeling mixture diffusion coefficients by entropy scaling is an unresolved task. We tackle this issue and present an entropy scaling framework for predicting mixture self-diffusion coefficients as well as mutual diffusion coefficients in a thermodynamically consistent way.

arxiv-2507-09178.title: The BdryMatérn GP: Reliable incorporation of boundary information on irregular domains for Gaussian process modeling
arxiv-2507-09178.creator: Liang Ding, Simon Mak, C. F. Jeff Wu
arxiv-2507-09178.description: Abstract Gaussian processes (GPs) are broadly used as surrogate models for expensive computer simulators of complex phenomena. However, a key bottleneck is that its training data are generated from this expensive simulator and thus can be highly limited. A promising solution is to supplement the learning model with boundary information from scientific knowledge.

pmc-10693032.title: DNA methylation profiles reveal sex-specific associations between gestational exposure to ambient air pollution and placenta cell-type composition in the PRISM cohort study
pmc-10693032.creator: Hachem Saddiki, Xueying Zhang, Elena Colicino, Ander Wilson, Itai Kloog, Robert O Wright, Rosalind J Wright, Corina Lesseur
pmc-10693032.description: BackgroundGestational exposure to ambient air pollution has been associated with adverse health outcomes for mothers and newborns. The placenta is a central regulator of the in utero environment that orchestrates development and postnatal life via fetal programming. Ambient air pollution contaminants can reach the placenta and have been shown to alter bulk placental tissue DNA methylation patterns.

pmc-11405689.title: CircRNA based multivalent neuraminidase vaccine induces broad protection against influenza viruses in mice
pmc-11405689.creator: Xinyu Yue, Cailing Zhong, Rui Cao, Sizhe Liu, Zhiran Qin, Lin Liu, Yanmei Zhai, Wanyu Luo, Yikai Lian, Mengjie Zhang, Hongjie Lu, Yuanyuan Wang, Mengxin Xu, Shuning Liu, Kexin Lv, Yuzhu Sun, Xingchen Zhu, Haoting Mai, Jing Liao, Jingyi Yang, Lei Deng, Yang Liu, Caijun Sun, Ke-Wei Zheng, Yuelong Shu,
pmc-11405689.description: Developing broad-spectrum influenza vaccines is crucial for influenza control and potential pandemic preparedness. Here, we reported a novel vaccine design utilizing circular RNA (circRNA) as a delivery platform for multi-subtype neuraminidases (NA) (influenza A N1, N2, and influenza B Victoria lineage NA) immunogens.

pmc-11738965.creator: Ayomipo Amiola, Verity Chester, Kiran Purandare, Rohit Shankar, Regi Alexander
pmc-11738965.description: AimsNHS England's ‘Transforming Care’ initiative introduced care and treatment reviews (CTRs) for adults with intellectual disabilities and/or autism to avoid inpatient admissions, improve inpatient care quality and support timely discharge. However, the complexity of the structural features that determine protein–protein interactions makes their design challenging. pmc-13213628.title: Cost savings associated with the adoption of lower-dose everolimus in patients with advanced neuroendocrine tumors
pmc-13213628.creator: G.R. de Almeida, R.P. Riechelmann, A.B. Brito, R.G. Taboada, A.L.M. da Silva, R.F. Weschenfelder, A.P.B.S. Etges
pmc-13213628.description: BackgroundEverolimus is effective in advanced neuroendocrine tumors (NETs) but is associated with substantial toxicity and high long-term costs. Real-world data suggest that lower doses (≤6 mg/day) achieve comparable efficacy with reduced toxicity compared with standard-dose therapy. This study aimed to quantify the cost savings associated with a lower-dose everolimus strategy in a middle-income country setting.

pmc-13369983.title: Urobiome composition varies with vesicoureteral reflux grade and history of febrile urinary tract infection
pmc-13369983.creator: Theresa C. Barrett, Kelvin Li, Adam Fitch, Asha Patel, Bhanu Sharma, Jacqueline Holden, Kermina Abdelsayed, Nina N. Kowalewski, Sridhar Narla, Daniel Bushnell, Barbara A. Methé, Catherine S. Forster
pmc-13369983.description: Vesicoureteral reflux (VUR) is a risk factor for urinary tract infection (UTI). However, data describing the urobiome in children with VUR are limited. Here, we characterized the urobiome in children with and without VUR to better understand its potential role in VUR pathogenesis. Catheterized urine samples were obtained from children who presented for voiding cystourethrogram (VCUG) between 12/1/2020 and 10/3/2023.

pmc-13564186.title: Synergistic Integration of Fe–N4 Single‐Atom Sites and Directionally Aligned Electrode Architecture for High‐Performance Lithium–Sulfur Batteries
pmc-13564186.creator: Lin Shen, Yijia Zou, Yuming Wang, Erya Gao, Christopher S Allen, Tianyi Zhang, Stephen J Skinner, Nigel P Brandon, Chun Huang
pmc-13564186.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Sluggish kinetics of redox reactions and slow ion transport restrict the performance of lithium‐sulfur (Li─S) batteries. Here, we fabricate cathodes containing vertically aligned porous structures hosting atomically dispersed Fe─N4 single‐atom catalyst (SAC) sites on graphitic carbon nitride (g‐C3N4). Density functional theory (DFT) calculations suggest that the Fe─N4 sites strengthen Li2S adsorption, optimize electronic structure, and lower the reaction energy change associated with liquid‐solid transition and Li2S oxidation.

pmc-13613897.title: A modular class-aware workflow for small RNA sequencing analysis using mouse sperm as a case study
pmc-13613897.creator: Da Lu, Huan Liao, Tishtar Daruwalla, Anthony J Hannan
pmc-13613897.description: BackgroundSmall RNA sequencing analysis is challenging because RNA classes differ in biogenesis, sequence redundancy, genomic organization, and annotation reliability. Integrated workflows accommodating these constraints remain limited, particularly for fragment-level and cluster-level analysis.MethodsWe present a reproducible, containerized, class-aware workflow for small RNA sequencing analysis, using mouse sperm as a case study.

pmc-13664169.title: Decade-Stratified Malignancy Risk in Hysteroscopic Polypectomy: A Multicenter Registry Analysis of 9269 Procedures
pmc-13664169.creator: Rina Tamir Yaniv, Tamar Tzur, Hila Goldstein, Gadi Ben-Shitrit, Gabi Haran
pmc-13664169.description: Simple SummaryAmong 9269 hysteroscopic polypectomies, endometrial malignancy rose from 0.45% in women under age 50 to 1.25% at ages 50–59, 3.79% at ages 60–69, and 4.58% at age 70 or older, reaching 8/61 (13.1%) in the oldest women with a documented postmenopausal bleeding (PMB) indication. Procedures coded with a non-PMB uterine bleeding indication were not associated with excess malignancy risk.

pmc-13676261.title: Life Participation in Parents of Children With CKD
pmc-13676261.creator: Anastasia Hughes, Andrea Matus Gonzalez, Anita van Zwieten, Chandana Guha, Simon Carter, Germaine Wong, Dale Coghlan, Amanda Dominello, Jonathan C Craig, Martin Howell, Siah Kim, Karine Manera, Colm O’Reilly, Javier Recabarren Silva, Angela Rejuso, Benedicte Sautenet, Nicole Scholes-Robertson, Amand
pmc-13676261.description: BackgroundThe caregiver burden among parents of children with chronic kidney disease (CKD) is high and can impair their life participation, which may in turn have negative consequences on their children’s care and outcomes. We aim to describe effects on life participation in parents of children with CKD, from the perspectives of their children, health professionals, and the parents themselves.
